journey.title: Attention and wonder
journey.subtitle: Three ways of seeing the living world
introduction: A cloud, a bird, a tiger: a small encounter can open into something larger. These poems invite us to look closely, then carry what we have seen into memory.
Begin with the quiet abundance of Wordsworth, listen to Dickinson’s inward song, and finish with Blake’s unanswered wonder.
closing: You have carried three different kinds of wonder through these poems. Their images can stay with you: a field of flowers, a small persistent bird, a creature burning in the dark.

note: Wordsworth begins with a passing sight and returns to it in solitude. Notice how the flowers become an inward resource: learning the poem gives its movement a home in your own memory.
Dickinson turns from an outward scene to an unseen companion. After Wordsworth’s dancing flowers, listen for a smaller movement: the song that continues without asking anything in return.
Blake’s tiger brings a different kind of attention. Its beauty leaves the speaker questioning rather than reassured. Let the repeated questions hold their mystery as you learn the poem.
